cards.explanation: The answer is what is going to happen to Him. Jesus takes the Twelve aside and begins to tell them what was going to happen to Him (Mark 10:32). He isn't handing out hotel info, friends. He's telling them the hard part ahead of time, and I think that takes a steady heart.

The answer is True. Jesus says the Son of Man will be delivered over to the chief priests and scribes, and "They will condemn Him to death…" (Mark 10:33). He says it straight, with no sugar on top. That's a heavy line, so I'll just say it plainly: this part is heavy.
The answer is three. Jesus says, "And after three days He will rise again." (Mark 10:34) The story doesn't end with the hard part, friends. I'd say that's the line worth holding onto.

The answer is True. James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come to Jesus and say, "Teacher, we want You to do for us whatever we ask." (Mark 10:35) They open with the blank check before they name the amount. Bold move, friends.

The answer is seats at His right and left. The two brothers say, "Grant that one of us may sit at Your right hand and the other at Your left in Your glory." (Mark 10:37) Two brothers, two seats. I've asked for plenty of things in my day, but never the best chairs in the house.
The answer is False. Jesus replies, "You do not know what you are asking…" (Mark 10:38). Then He asks about the cup and the baptism. They had a request, but they didn't see the whole picture.

The answer is "We can." The brothers answer, "We can" (Mark 10:39). That's their whole reply. Jesus then tells them, "You will drink the cup that I drink…" and they will be baptized with His baptism (Mark 10:39).

The answer is that the seats are not His to grant. Jesus says, "But to sit at My right or left is not Mine to grant. These seats belong to those for whom they have been prepared." (Mark 10:40) Granting them is not His to do. I'd say James and John got a plain answer.

The answer is that the ten were angry with them. "When the ten heard about this, they became indignant with James and John." (Mark 10:41) Indignant means upset, and the text says it directly, friends. That's the feeling the text gives for the ten.

The answer is that they lord it over them. Jesus says, "You know that those regarded as rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their superiors exercise authority over them." (Mark 10:42) The Gentiles are people who aren't Israelites. He starts with what they already see around them.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "But it shall not be this way among you." (Mark 10:43) He's pointing the Twelve toward a different way. Then He tells them what that way looks like.

The answer is servant. "Instead, whoever wants to become great among you must be your servant…" (Mark 10:43). Greatness shows up in serving, and Jesus says it plainly, friends. Servant is the word He picks.

The answer is slave. Jesus says, "…and whoever wants to be first must be the slave of all." (Mark 10:44) He goes even lower than servant, and that's the point. That's what He asks of whoever wants to be first.
The answer is to serve. Jesus says, "For even the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve…" (Mark 10:45). He says it about Himself. Serving is what He came to do.

The answer is True. Jesus says the Son of Man came "…to give His life as a ransom for many." (Mark 10:45) That's the name He uses for Himself (Mark 2:10). I'd call it the biggest line in the passage, friends.
